title: Witness and Verdict
premise: Mirabel Winterbourne, the cathedral archivist who has quietly unraveled three 'accidental' deaths the police misfiled, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after old verger Aldous Crane's funeral — signed by a witness everyone insists died decades ago in the crypt fire. Following the letter's liturgical ciphers through the cathedral's sealed records, Mirabel discovers the witness, Edith Vane, faked her death to escape a conspiracy of inheritance fraud that Crane's death threatens to expose. The letter was a dying message, and its sender — the last conspirator, the cathedral's beloved canon — is hunting for Edith before she can testify. In the crypt's locked annex, Mirabel finds Edith alive, confronts the canon as he comes to finish his work, and forces a confession recorded on the cathedral's own restoration equipment, ending the conspiracy and giving Edith back her name.
about_author: Bram Eriksen is the pen name of a former parish records clerk from the Norfolk coast who spent eleven years cataloguing church archives before turning to crime fiction. His novels are known for their quiet ecclesiastical settings, meticulous archival detail, and detectives who listen more than they speak.

chapters.title: Postmarked Ashes
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Three days after verger Aldous Crane's funeral, an envelope arrives bearing a confession and a postmark dated the day after the burial — impossible, since its signer, Edith Vane, died in the crypt fire forty years ago. Mirabel, who has solved three deaths the police called accidents, feels the old pattern stir. Emotional beat: the thrill and dread of a puzzle that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. He petitions the chapter to reopen the sealed crypt, ostensibly to check fire damage; inside, he finds Crane's own notebook hidden behind a memorial plaque, half in cipher. The notebook suggests Crane died knowing something about the Vane inheritance. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion — Crane was a friend, and friends don't usually hide evidence.

chapters.title: A Death Well Filed
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Reviewing the coroner's file, Mirabel notes Crane's fall matches none of the stair's wear patterns, and a witness statement from canon Ambrose Fell feels rehearsed. Detective Inspector Sallow warns him off, weary of Mirabel's unsolicited successes. Emotional beat: loneliness of the amateur — being right and unwelcome.

chapters.title: What the Registers Keep
chapters.summary: POV Edith (interleaved fragments of her hidden testimony). Flashbacks reveal the 1980s inheritance scheme: a family fortune laundered through the cathedral's restoration fund, Edith the bookkeeper who was meant to die in the 'accidental' crypt fire. Emotional beat: fear preserved in amber — memory as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: The Canon's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Canon Fell, warm and helpful, offers Mirabel access to old records — access that conveniently omits the restoration-fund years. Mirabel plays along, cataloguing Fell's small evasions. A second threatening letter arrives, warning him the witness is dead and must stay dead. Emotional beat: the horror of realizing the killer is the most beloved man in the building.

chapters.title: Cipher of Hours
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Decoding Crane's notebook using the liturgical hours as a key, Mirabel learns Crane had contacted Edith before his death — and that she answered, meaning she is alive and someone knew. The letter's postmark date now reads as a taunt: the sender wanted Mirabel pulled in. Emotional beat: vertigo — he isn't the hunter; he's the lure.

chapters.title: Sallow's Doubt
chapters.summary: POV Sallow. The DI, unable to ignore Mirabel's stair analysis, quietly reopens the file and finds Crane's fall was staged with a rope burn the first investigation missed. He and Mirabel form an uneasy alliance, each distrusting the other's methods. Emotional beat: reluctant trust — two solitary men discovering the value of a second witness.

chapters.title: The Name Restored
chapters.summary: POV Edith. Living under a borrowed name as a lay steward in a neighboring parish, Edith realizes Crane's death means the conspirators are closing the ledger — and she is its last line. She decides to come out of hiding, leaving a trail only an archivist would read. Emotional beat: resolve — choosing testimony over survival.

chapters.title: Vespers in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Following Edith's archival trail, Mirabel reaches the crypt annex during vespers, finding her alive — just as Canon Fell arrives, intending to seal them both in and burn the records. A standoff in the dark among the coffers of the fraudulent dead. Emotional beat: terror and clarity — the archive becomes a trap, then a shield.

chapters.title: Witness and Verdict
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel and Edith. The cathedral's restoration microphones, left running, capture Fell's confession as Mirabel stalls him with questions about the fund's ledger; Sallow arrives with the coroner's reopened file. Fell is taken; Edith signs her true name to her testimony, ending forty years of exile. Emotional beat: belonging — a woman and an archivist, both keepers of buried things, finally heard.
